title: Direct image of etale sheaves of modules over a constant ring: module structure, additive and left exact
statement: Let $u:U\to V$ be a morphism of schemes [def-pc-scheme] and $R$ a commutative ring. For a scheme $T$ let $T_{\Et}$ be its small etale site [def-weil-pbc-etale-site], $\Ab(T_{\Et})$ the category of abelian sheaves on it [def-weil-pbc-abelian-etale-sheaves], $R_T$ the constant sheaf of rings with value $R$ on $T_{\Et}$ [def-weil-pbc-constant-sheaf] and $\Mod(T_{\Et},R)$ the abelian category of sheaves of $R_T$-modules [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category]. For a sheaf $G$ of abelian groups or of commutative rings on $U_{\Et}$ let $u_*G$ be the sheaf $W\mapsto G(W\times_VU)$ on $V_{\Et}$, $W\times_VU$ the fibre product [def-pc-fibre-product], with restriction along $g:W_1\to W_2$ that of $G$ along $g\times\mathrm{id}_U$ (a sheaf of the same kind by [lem-weil-pbc-etale-base-change-continuous]). Let $\rho:R_V\to u_*R_U$ be the morphism of sheaves of rings which, by the universal property of sheafification [def-weil-pbc-sheafification], extends the morphism from the constant presheaf of rings with value $R$ on $V_{\Et}$ to $u_*R_U$ whose component at $W$ is the map $R\to R_U(W\times_VU)$ of the sheafification morphism of the constant presheaf $R$ on $U_{\Et}$. Then: (1) for $F\in\Mod(U_{\Et},R)$ the abelian sheaf $u_*F$, with the action $R_V(W)\times F(W\times_VU)\to F(W\times_VU)$, $(a,s)\mapsto\rho_W(a)\,s$, is a sheaf of $R_V$-modules, and for an $R_U$-linear morphism $\varphi:F\to F'$ the morphism $u_*\varphi$, $(u_*\varphi)_W=\varphi_{W\times_VU}$, is $R_V$-linear; this defines a functor $u_*:\Mod(U_{\Et},R)\to\Mod(V_{\Et},R)$ whose composite with the forgetful functor to $\Ab(V_{\Et})$ is the composite of the forgetful functor to $\Ab(U_{\Et})$ with $u_*:\Ab(U_{\Et})\to\Ab(V_{\Et})$; (2) this functor is additive and left exact [def-sp-left-exact-additive]: it preserves finite products and kernels, so for every exact sequence $0\to F_1\to F_2\to F_3$ of $\Mod(U_{\Et},R)$ the sequence $0\to u_*F_1\to u_*F_2\to u_*F_3$ is exact in $\Mod(V_{\Et},R)$.

proof.text: Put B(W)=W\times_VU. The continuity lemma makes u_*R_U a sheaf of rings and u_*F a sheaf of abelian groups. The maps R\to R_U(B(W)) commute with restrictions, since they are components of the constant-presheaf sheafification morphism. Hence they give a morphism of ring presheaves from the constant presheaf R to u_*R_U. The universal property of the constant sheaf R_V (sheafification in rings) extends this uniquely to a morphism of ring sheaves \rho:R_V\to u_*R_U. In particular \rho_{W_1}(a|_{W_1})=\rho_{W_2}(a)|_{B(W_1)} for every g:W_1\to W_2 and a\in R_V(W_2).

proof.text: For a\in R_V(W) and s\in F(B(W)), define a\cdot s=\rho_W(a)s. The module axioms follow by substituting the ring homomorphism \rho_W into the R_U(B(W))-module axioms. For g:W_1\to W_2, semilinearity of F and naturality of \rho give (\rho_{W_2}(a)s)|_{B(W_1)}=\rho_{W_1}(a|_{W_1})s|_{B(W_1)}. Thus the underlying abelian sheaf u_*F with this action is an R_V-module sheaf. If \varphi is R_U-linear, then \varphi_{B(W)}(\rho_W(a)s)=\rho_W(a)\varphi_{B(W)}(s), so u_*\varphi is R_V-linear. Identities and compositions hold componentwise. Forgetting the action leaves exactly F(B(W)) and \varphi_{B(W)}, proving the claimed equality of composites with forgetful functors.

source.place: Tag 03CV, definition-sheaf-modules; pushforward construction preceding Tag 03DC, lemma-exactness-pushforward-pullback

proof.text: Addition of module-sheaf morphisms is componentwise, since the sum of two linear maps is linear and its restrictions commute. Consequently (u_*(\varphi+\psi))_W=(\varphi+\psi)_{B(W)}=\varphi_{B(W)}+\psi_{B(W)}=(u_*\varphi+u_*\psi)_W, and u_*0=0. This proves additivity on morphisms.

source.place: Tag 03D9, section-kernels, paragraph defining addition on morphisms

proof.text: Apply the sectionwise module-sheaf limits lemma on U_Et with O=R_U and on V_Et with O=R_V. For a finite family (F_i), its product has sections \prod_i F_i(B(W)) and componentwise scalar action. The canonical comparison u_*(\prod_i F_i)\to\prod_i u_*F_i is therefore the identity on these tuples at W, and both R_V(W)-actions send (s_i)_i to (\rho_W(a)s_i)_i. It is an isomorphism of module sheaves, including for the empty product, whose sections are zero. For \varphi:F\to F^{\prime}, the same lemma computes its kernel sectionwise: both u_*(\ker\varphi)(W) and (\ker u_*\varphi)(W) are {s\in F(B(W)): \varphi_{B(W)}(s)=0}, with the same restrictions and scalar action. The canonical kernel comparison is thus an isomorphism of module sheaves. This proves preservation of finite products and kernels.

By the definition of left exact additive functor, step 4 gives left exactness. Explicitly, an exact sequence $0\to F_1\xrightarrow{a}F_2\xrightarrow{b}F_3$ identifies $a$ with a kernel of $b$: the induced map $F_1\to\ker b$ is an isomorphism. A functor sends an isomorphism and its inverse to inverse maps. Applying $u_*$ to this identification and composing with the canonical kernel comparison isomorphism of step 4 therefore identifies $u_*a$ with the kernel inclusion of $u_*b$. This is precisely exactness of $0\to u_*F_1\to u_*F_2\to u_*F_3$.
